title: The Battle of the Bulge
photoNote: A German soldier in a rubberized motorcyclist's coat points the way forward beside a German Sd.Kfz. 251 halftrack, with a soldier in a Waffen-SS camouflage smock at right. German photo from captured film, held by the U.S. National Archives, 208-AA-202B-4 (naId 12010183), NARA's own copy. NARA dates it 16 Dec 1944 in the Belgian sector and calls the vehicle an American halftrack; it is German, and the roll is generally placed at the Poteau crossroads near Recht about 18 Dec 1944, with 1st SS Panzer Division troops. Historians note parts of this sequence were staged for the camera, so captions state facts plainly and never present it as the opening minute. Allowed under Brian's 19 Nov 2026 rule for captured German photos held by NARA. Colorized by WW2 Dispatches on 19 Nov 2026 in the C2 Kodachrome look (flash/colorize-2026-12-16-the-bulge.py; notes in flash/colors-2026-12-16-the-bulge.md). The flash/ art is the full card: framing set below.
photoCredit: A German soldier in the Ardennes offensive, December 1944. German photo, captured, U.S. National Archives (208-AA-202B-4). Colorized by WW2 Dispatches.
_note: Prepared 19 Nov 2026 for the Wednesday 9 Dec 2026 research run. Research copies this record into dispatches/ (same id), adds num, facts, sources, themes, film, kind, and videoPhotos, and never changes the fields above (Research doc, Flash days). Instagram carousel leads (real black and white archival photos, never a second colorized image): NARA 111-SC-198304, two survivors of the overrun 110th Infantry in Bastogne, 19 Dec 1944; NARA 111-SC-253861, the 101st Airborne on the road out of Bastogne to stem the German drive, 19 Dec 1944; NARA 111-SC-200487, the 82nd Airborne marching through fog near Werbomont, 20 Dec 1944; NARA 208-YE-99, German photo, captured, U.S. National Archives: grenadiers pass a burning American vehicle (same roll as the card). Suggested caption hook: "At 5:30 a.m. on 16 December 1944, the quietest stretch of the American front exploded." The noon Living Card should not end on the Poteau film from The Enemy Strikes, since this card comes from the same crossroads.
